subsystems.name: Collector swarm
subsystems.role: millions to trillions of independent sun-facing units that capture starlight; unlike a solid shell, each orbits freely, because no known material could hold a rigid sphere around a star.
parts: thin-film mirrors or lightweight photovoltaic film
local radiator to shed waste heat

subsystems.name: Material supply chain
subsystems.role: supplies the mass needed, since a swarm's total area is measured in planetary surfaces' worth.
parts: robotic mining of asteroids or a small moon
feedstock for thin-film and structural parts

subsystems.name: In-space manufacturing and assembly base
subsystems.role: turns raw rock and metal into finished collectors without launching them from Earth.

subsystems.name: Coordination and control
subsystems.role: keeps billions of independent units from colliding, pointing and orbiting together.

subsystems.name: Energy transport
subsystems.role: moves captured energy to where it is used, whether a planet, a fleet, or local industry.
parts: or direct use on site for computation and manufacturing

subsystems.name: Thermal rejection
subsystems.role: all captured energy ends as low-grade heat, so the swarm must radiate it away as infrared — the physical signature that would give it away.
parts: wavelength management to stay cool enough to function

buildSteps.title: Prove robotic resource use off Earth
buildSteps.detail: Send robots to a near-Earth asteroid or a small moon to dig, crush and separate material. Sample-return missions have already brought asteroid and lunar material back; extraction and refining in space have not been done at scale.

buildSteps.title: Refine and form material in vacuum
buildSteps.detail: Use concentrated sunlight or a small reactor to melt metal and draw glassy or metallic film. Microgravity additive manufacturing has been demonstrated on the ISS; refining whole tonnes of asteroid rock has not.

buildSteps.title: Build a production base off Earth
buildSteps.detail: Site fabrication where the material is, so nothing has to climb out of Earth's gravity well. Launch finished collectors with electromagnetic mass drivers or similar low-gravity launchers, none of which has yet been built at this scale.

buildSteps.title: Automate the whole loop
buildSteps.detail: Mining, refining, forming and launching must run with minimal human input, because the numbers involved vastly exceed what crews can assemble by hand. Self-replicating machinery in the von Neumann sense remains theory.

buildSteps.title: Deploy the first ring of collectors
buildSteps.detail: Release units into orbits that avoid each other and shadow one another, each doing its own station-keeping and pointing.

buildSteps.title: Scale up incrementally
buildSteps.detail: Grow collector count as production capacity compounds, so the swarm is built in decades-to-millennia steps rather than in one campaign.

buildSteps.title: Deliver energy and manage heat
buildSteps.detail: Beam power to receivers, or consume it locally, while every unit radiates waste heat away as infrared.

prerequisites.why: reusable rockets have cut launch prices, but a swarm needs materials moved on a scale no launch industry has approached.
sample returns and small experiments exist; sustained mining and smelting of asteroid or lunar material has never been done.
long-duration space robots work today, but not at the scale, lifetime or independence a swarm requires.

prerequisites.tech: Wireless power beaming at power-plant scale
prerequisites.why: microwave and laser power transfer has been demonstrated at kilowatt scale in tests, not at gigawatt scale over orbital distances.
exponential growth of the collector population is what makes a swarm feasible at all, and no such machine exists.
thermodynamics forces the swarm to radiate most captured energy as infrared; managing that without cooking the collectors is unsolved.

pathway.milestone: robotic asteroid and lunar sample returns, microgravity manufacturing experiments, and space-based solar power studies
pathway.unlocks: the basic building blocks, none yet at industrial scale.

pathway.milestone: robotic extraction, refining and assembly off Earth, plus a pilot power satellite returning useful power to a planet
steady growth of independent collectors in solar orbit, starting with a partial ring
pathway.unlocks: a measurable fraction of a star's output, harvestable without a solid shell.

pathway.milestone: a swarm large enough to change a star's apparent brightness and infrared output
pathway.unlocks: a star-scale energy supply — and, since it would be visible in infrared, a searchable signature. The dimming of the star KIC 8462852 was once considered a possible sign, but natural dust is the accepted explanation.
